muse.fix: Section ISA §7.3 (new paragraph after the device table) and §10. The diff should add to §7.3 the sentence: 'Device-model state belongs to the loaded program like classical memory (§7.1): the console byte sequence, the clock counter c and the block sector map are established at load from their initial values (the block map from layout.block_image, K10) and persist across runs, changed only by effect execution and by reversal (§7.4, T4); closing a run does not reinitialise them. The entropy position p is per-run state: it starts at 0 over the entropy tape copied at that bennett_run (§10). The effect tape is per-run.' And in the §10 addition, replace 'initialization is never repeated merely to start a run' with 'the §7.1/§7.3 program-lifetime state is never reinitialised merely to start a run'. Corrected expected values for the new vectors: run A clock.read writes 0 (c becomes 1), COMPLETED, CLOSED unreversed; run B clock.read MUST write 1; if A is REVERSED before CLOSED, B writes 0. Run A block.write sector 2 then CLOSED unreversed; run B block.read sector 2 returns A's bytes; with A reversed, sector 2 is absent again and reads 512 zero bytes. Two ways out exist: (a) program-lifetime device state as above (recommended: matches T4 entry-value restoration, the block-as-disk device model of north-star rungs 3/6, and the proposal's own persistence principle); (b) per-run reinitialisation of all device state stated explicitly in §7.3 — viable but then the §10 sentence must be scoped to §7.1 state and the dialect/VM must not assume a persistent block device across entries. I would take (a).

steps.by: clause:ISA-7.3 device table (State (initial): console empty, clock c=0, entropy p=0, block map from block_image); clause:ISA-10 (entropy tape copied at bennett_run, per-run; bennett_tape_open by run id)
steps.claim: Device models have observable state with stated initial values but no stated lifetime; the entropy tape (hence position p) is supplied per run, while clock c and the block sector map are readable by later runs.

steps.by: witness:adg recommended diff (dossier part adg, 'Recommended exact spec diff')
steps.claim: The adg diff pins load-time establishment and cross-run persistence only for classical memory, allocation table, bump pointer (§7.1) and the register ledger (§3.3); its §10 sentence 'initialization is never repeated merely to start a run' does not name device state, and read maximally it would also freeze the per-run entropy position.

steps.by: witness:sequential R entries on one loaded program: run A executes clock.read (writes 0, c=1) and block.write to an absent sector, COMPLETED then CLOSED without reversal; run B executes clock.read and block.read of that sector
steps.claim: On this input a persistence-reading executor returns clock=1 and A's sector bytes; a reinitialisation-reading executor returns clock=0 and 512 zero bytes. Both readings conform to the amended text.

Conclusion: the defect adg exists to repair (load-time vs per-run initialisation) remains observable for clock and block after the diff is applied, and the unqualified §10 sentence is inconsistent for entropy p; two conformant executors compute different results (S0).
